1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4	* Always update docs/USER_GUIDE.md if something changed.
5	
6	## Repository Overview
7	
8	Andes hybrid RISC-V co-simulator: QEMU 9.x (functional, MHz-level) + vsim (SystemC + Verilator, cycle-accurate) share architectural state across a magic-CSR boundary. The system runs a three-phase round-trip: **QEMU1** (drain on CSR/PC trigger) -> **vsim** (resume + execute + drain) -> **QEMU2** (restore via gdbstub, continue).
9	
10	Two Git submodules:
11	- `QEMU/` - QEMU fork hosting the TCG plugin (branch: `hybrid`)
12	- `verilator/` - vsim sources; `hybrid/` subdirs hold the plugin and test fixtures
13	- `tools/simpoint/` - SimPoint 3.2 (UCSD) clustering binary; pinned to upstream `17783e5`
14	
15	Shared ABI lives at `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (not inside either submodule).
16	
17	## Build Commands
18	
19	**Primary path (`./hsim`)** -- the end-user driver, used in all user-facing docs:
20	
21	```sh
22	./hsim build                       # builds qemu, vsim, plugin, simpoint, fixtures
23	./hsim test                        # full e2e suite (defaults: MODE=both, JOBS=8)
24	./hsim run <elf> --mode csr|pc|icount|slice  # one round-trip
25	./hsim list <fixtures|modes>
26	```
27	
28	**Developer escape hatch** -- the underlying scripts. Use these when
29	working on the build system, the harness, or a single leg in isolation:
30	
31	```sh
32	# Build everything (qemu -> vsim -> plugin -> simpoint)
33	source ./setup.sh
34	
35	# Build individual components
36	./scripts/build_qemu.sh                              # QEMU (configure + make -j64)
37	./scripts/build_vsim.sh                              # vsim (Docker/podman, runs ./build.sh inside container)
38	make -C qemu_plugin QEMU_ROOT=./QEMU  # TCG plugin (out-of-tree)
39	./scripts/build_simpoint.sh                          # SimPoint clustering binary (g++ on host)
40	
41	# Build RISC-V ELF test fixtures
42	make -C tests/fixtures              # all fixtures
43	make -C tests/fixtures rt_c_v_regs.elf  # single fixture
44	
45	# Clean
46	source ./setup.sh clean [qemu|vsim|plugin|simpoint|all]
47	```
48	
49	**Outputs:**
50	- `build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64`
51	- `verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium` (or other CPU variant)
52	- `qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so`
53	- `tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint`
54	
55	`scripts/build_vsim.sh` is Docker-based (podman). It builds an image from `verilator/Dockerfile` (target `env`) then runs `./build.sh` inside it, mounting the repo at `/work` and `include/` as `/include:ro`.
56	
57	## Running Tests
58	
59	```sh
60	# All e2e tests in parallel (auto-detects job count from nproc + /dev/shm headroom)
61	bash scripts/run_e2e.sh
62	
63	# Run with specific options
64	JOBS=4 MODE=csr bash scripts/run_e2e.sh         # 4-way parallel, CSR-mode only
65	JOBS=1 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh                  # sequential (debug)
66	FILTER=rt_c_v bash scripts/run_e2e.sh           # regex filter on fixture name
67	LOG_DIR=/tmp/my-logs bash scripts/run_e2e.sh    # custom log directory
68	
69	# Unit tests (inside vsim build container)
70	# The container build runs: cmake --build build -j
71	# To run ctest directly after build:
72	#   podman run ... ./build.sh && podman exec ... ctest --test-dir build -L hybrid-e2e
73	```
74	
75	**Important:** on a high-core-count machine (128+ cores) `default_jobs()` computes `min(nproc, /dev/shm_free/256MB)` which can reach 128+. Running that many vsim Verilator processes simultaneously saturates CPU and causes timeouts. Use `JOBS=8` (or lower) as a practical cap: `JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh`.
76	
77	`scripts/run_e2e.sh` exits 0 only when all tests pass. Logs go to a `mktemp` directory under `/tmp`; path is printed at the start of each run. Each test's full output lands in `$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log`.
78	
79	**Manual driver tests**: `tests/hsim/test_hsim_*.sh` are per-feature RED-then-green smoke tests for `./hsim` subcommands (F1..F14). They are run manually during driver development, not wired into `scripts/run_e2e.sh`. Each script is self-contained (sources `setup.sh` artifacts, runs one subcommand, asserts on stdout). The same convention applies to `tests/plugin/test_plugin_*.sh` (QEMU-plugin-only smoke tests).
80	
81	## Architecture
82	
83	### Three-Phase Handoff
84	
85	```
86	QEMU1 --(state file)--> vsim --(state file + V-scratch mmap)--> QEMU2
87	```
88	
89	1. **QEMU plugin** (`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`) - TCG plugin. On CSR-write trigger (`csrwi 0x7C0, 0`) or PC-trigger, drains QEMU's architectural state into a binary `hybrid_state_v1` struct written to `--outfile`.
90	2. **vsim handoff controller** (`src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp`) - Detects the trigger inside vsim, pauses the hart via DMI, then calls `ResumeDriver` to restore state.
91	3. **ResumeDriver** (`src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`) - Writes GPRs/FPRs/CSRs/V-state into the vsim hart via RISC-V Debug Module Abstract Commands and Program Buffer.
92	4. **StateDrain** (`src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp`) - On vsim exit trigger, reads back the full architectural state via DMI Abstract Commands.
93	5. **qemu_handback** (`src/hybrid/qemu_handback.hpp`) - Spawns QEMU2, connects via gdbstub, sends P-packet register writes for GPRs/FPRs/CSRs/V-regs, then `continue`s.
94	
95	**CSR restore split**: `ResumeDriver` writes only the CSRs that the vsim phase can touch: `mstatus`, `mtvec`, `mcycle`, `minstret`. The QEMU plugin still drains the full M-mode set (`mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mscratch`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`, `mip`, `mie`, `satp`) plus PMP (64 `pmpaddr` + 16 `pmpcfg`) into `hybrid_state_v1`, but those are restored only on QEMU2 via the gdbstub P-packet path in `qemu_handback`. The vsim phase is assumed trap-free and PMP-static; if a future workload needs traps or dynamic PMP inside the ROI, `ResumeDriver` must be extended.
96	
97	### Trigger Modes
98	
99	The repo ships 4 switching modes, split by what they profile.
100	
101	Kernel modes (measure one region you choose):
102	- **CSR mode** (default): Pattern-matches `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` (entry) / `csrwi 0x7C0, 1` (exit) at retire time. CSR 0x7C0 is a benign vendor write on Andes ax45mp.
103	- **PC mode**: explicit boundary PCs passed as `--pc-start S --pc-end E` (symbol name or `0x` address) resolved at startup; CSR insns are bypassed. Both args are required.
104	
105	Whole-program modes (sample by instruction count):
106	- **icount mode**: single boundary on each leg - plugin `icount=N` fast-forwards QEMU1, vsim `--hybrid-icount M` measures the window and drains. No markers, no warmup; for CSR-less workloads.
107	- **SimPoint-driven mode**: profile the run into slices (interval = insns per slice), cluster representative phases, measure each phase like icount, weight-combine into a whole-program cycle estimate. Drive via `./hsim run --mode simpoint` (or the equivalent `./hsim estimate`). The bbv-profile / archive / replay machinery are its stages, not separate modes.
108	
109	`./hsim run --mode csr|pc|icount|simpoint` is the unified orchestrator; `tests/e2e.sh` drives csr/pc internally. Each yields a cycle figure: kernel/window cycles = the vsim `mcycle` delta (`hybrid_state_v1::mcycle`); SimPoint reports the weight-combined `estimated_cycles`.
110	
111	### Shared ABI (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`)
112	
113	`hybrid_state_v1` is the binary wire format exchanged between QEMU plugin, vsim, and the handback path. It holds: 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs, M-mode CSRs (mstatus, mepc, etc.), PMP (64 pmpaddr + 16 pmpcfg), and the V extension block (vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, 32 vreg[], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr). `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX=64` supports VLEN up to 512 bits. Multi-byte fields are little-endian (native on RV64 + x86-64 host); the format is not endian-portable.
114	
115	Flags (`HYBRID_FLAG_RV64`, `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`, `HYBRID_FLAG_V`) gate which state blocks are live. The ABI struct is validated by `verilator/tests/hybrid/state_abi.test.cpp`.
116	
117	### V-State Transport
118	
119	V data registers (v0..v31) move through a fixed scratch region
120	(`kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000` on `-M andes_ae350`) in the shared mmap. vsim drives

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
